The project examines how to assess and guide the social impact of innovation in organisations and mobility systems. It combines two research areas: workplace diversity and inclusion strategies, focusing on equal opportunities, participation and organisational well-being; and the adoption of smart electric mobility solutions, considering socioeconomic benefits, industrial effects and sustainability. The research project focuses on the fluid-dynamic and thermal study and optimization of a Thermal Energy Storage (TES) system based on Phase Change Materials (PCM), using air as the heat transfer fluid. The objective is to develop and validate transient Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) simulation models to analyze the charging (melting) and discharging (solidification) processes of the PCM. The study will evaluate different heat exchanger geometries and operating air parameters to overcome the low thermal conductivity limitation of PCMs, thereby maximizing heat transfer efficiency.
